services.cms: Node.js Docker runtime, single process on 127.0.0.1:1989
services.k6: grafana/k6 v2.1.0 (linux/arm64 container; image pinned by digest)
services.rateLimit: disabled for load-items and load-deliver to measure endpoint capacity

workloads.items: load-items.js, list ramp 1->50 VUs plus 10 VU detail and 30 VU create burst, 2m. List uses offset pagination (offset 0..4*limit). Detail reads ONE fixed seeded id (DETAIL_ITEM_ID, default I00000100000100000000) for reproducibility — so item_detail_duration_ms is a hot-row read served from the Postgres buffer cache, not a random read across 100k rows. Do not compare it against a future random-read workload.

notes: Postgres host port 55432 was used because an unrelated directus_postgres container already occupied host port 5432; the container service itself remains on 5432.
The generated JWT was passed through the shell only and is not stored in the repository.
Failed thresholds are retained as measurements, not replaced with estimates. load-deliver showed resource saturation under this single-process setup; see load-deliver.json.
pg_stat_statements was not available in the standard postgres:16-alpine container, so query-attribution follow-up remains open.
